chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father wrote in his bequest that I should enshroud him in three garments: one of them is a cloak of his which he used to pray in on Friday, and another garment, and a shirt. So I said to my father, 'Why do you write this?' He said, 'I fear that the people might overpower you, and if they say, 'Enshroud him in four or five,' do not do it. And wrap me with a turban, and do not count the turban as part of the enshrouding; rather, what is counted is what the body is wrapped with.'

key_terms.يُلَفُّ بِهِ الْجَسَدُ: What the body is wrapped with

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the number of garments for enshrouding the deceased and how is the turban treated?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imams' emphasis on adhering strictly to the Sunnah to prevent *bid'ah* (innovation) through popular custom, specifically limiting the shroud to three pieces as a practical safeguard against social pressure. It clarifies the juristic distinction between items that wrap the body versus those merely worn on the head, a nuance critical in Shia fiqh for determining the minimum obligatory shroud. This instruction reflects the broader Shia principle of simplicity in death rituals while maintaining dignity, rooted in the Prophet's practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umyer, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Myasws fatherasws wrote in hisasws bequest that Iasws should enshroud himasws in three clothes – one of them being a cloak of hisasws which heasws used to pray Salaat in on the day of Friday, and another cloth, and a shirt. So Iasws said to myasws fatherasws, ‘Why did youasws write this?’ So heasws said: ‘Out of fear that the people might overcome you and if they were to say, ‘Shroud himasws in four, or five (clothes)’, do not do it, and turban measws with a turban, and do not count the turban as being from the shroud. But rather, count what the body is wrapped with’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote in his will to me to shroud him with three pieces of cloth, one was a gown made in Hibarah with which he performed Salah (prayer) on Fridays and another piece of cloth, and a shirt. I asked my father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, “Why do you write these things?” He (the Imam) replied, “I am afraid people will overpower you. If they said to use four or five pieces, do not do so. Prepare a turban for me but turban is not counted as part of shroud. It is prepared to wrap the body therewith.’””
